tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description:
Get the top-ranked prediction market traders (grades S, A, B only). By default in the board's own rank order; sort, dir and activity reorder and scope the same wallets as the site's leaderboard does. Supports cursor pagination and optional filters.

Args:
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20): Max results per page
  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor from previous response; it is bound to the sort, dir and activity it was read with
  - category (string, optional): Filter by a sport or esports bucket (case-insensitive) such as Basketball or Esports, or sports for every sport but Esports. Omit it for every sports and esports wallet
  - strategy (string, optional): Trading style: two_sided, category_focused, high_activity, diversified, mixed, unclassified
  - sort (string, optional): rank (default), grade, volume (sports and esports USD volume), predictions, pnl, win_rate (wallets with at least 5 decided markets), edge (price_edge.edge, wallets whose edge ranks); a missing value sorts lowest
  - dir (string, optional): asc or desc; omitted, rank 1 first for rank and largest first for the rest
  - activity (string, optional): all (default), active (last trade 30 days ago or less) or inactive

Returns: Ranked list of traders with grade, score, sports and esports P&L, markets, win rate, edge over the price paid, and strategy. tools.name: get_trader
tools.description:
Look up a prediction market trader by wallet address or username. Returns grade (S through F), the edge over the price paid the profile badge shows (price_edge), and the sports and esports record: realized P&L (pnl.in_scope), markets traded, win rate, and volume. Under 5 decided markets stats.win_rate_status is not_enough_data: read stats.markets_won of stats.markets_decided, not win_rate as a rate. Wallet figures cover sports and esports markets only.

Optional expand fields for heavier data:
- strategy: Trading strategy classification
- categories: Per-category performance breakdown
- quant_metrics: retired since 2026-10-27; accepted and never returned, because its metrics covered every market of the wallet. Read pnl.in_scope or get_trader_pnl for the sports and esports record
- trust: Per-field provenance (source, freshness, reconciliation, completeness) for grade, P&L, and stats
- breakdowns: The profile's strategy breakdowns over sports and esports markets: P&L and win rate by UTC hour of first trade, hold-time and hour-of-day bands, risk metrics with category concentration, and entry-price buckets with their coverage (the settled positions the buckets leave out, such as two-sided hedges, by reason, count and P&L; its per-market P&L sum differs from pnl.in_scope.realized_pnl, which is Polymarket's published figure). Computed on the request, so slower for large wallets

A wallet address with no trader yet returns sync_status "unknown" (not an error). A username or trader id that matches no trader is a not_found error.

Args:
  - address (string, required): Ethereum wallet address (0x...) or trader username
  - expand (string[], optional): Heavy fields to include: "strategy", "categories", "trust", "breakdowns" ("quant_metrics" is accepted and returns nothing)
  - max_age_s (integer, optional, 0 or more): Freshness ceiling in seconds. The call answers only when data_quality.status is fresh or stale and data_quality.as_of is no older than this; otherwise it fails with reason freshness_ceiling_unsatisfied (HTTP 409). Nothing is refreshed to meet it

Returns: Trader profile with grade, P&L, stats, and optional expanded fields. The trader carries data_quality: status, as_of (the oldest clock the body rests on) and field_groups. fresh and stale both mean tracked and clocked; stale means as_of is older than max_age_s, the refresh budget of the group writer. Neither is a tolerance: compare as_of with your own. unknown means this read cannot date that group, never that it is recent.

tools.name: get_large_trades
tools.description:
Get recent large trades from graded prediction market traders. Each trade includes a 0-1 review score, persisted suspicion facts, trader grade, and market context. Cursor-paginated, newest first.

Args:
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20): Max results per page
  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor from previous response
  - min_size (number, default 5000): Minimum trade size in USD
  - category (string, optional): Filter by market category (case-insensitive): a sport such as Basketball, a league such as NBA (it folds into its sport), Esports, or sports for every sport but Esports. Omit it for every sports and esports trade
  - min_grade (string, optional): Minimum trader grade now (S, A, B, C, D, F); not with min_grade_at_trade
  - min_grade_at_trade (string, optional): Minimum grade the trader held when the trade filled (graded only), the basis the stream and webhooks share; not with min_grade
  - suspicious_only (boolean, optional): Keep only flagged trades; false preserves the current result set
  - min_market_volume_share (number, 0-1, optional): Keep only trades whose market_volume_share is known and at least this; a fraction, so 0.01 is one percent of the market's traded volume
  - sort (string, optional): "recent" (default, newest first) or "market_volume_share" (biggest share of its market first, over the last 30 days, or from the from bound on the history tools; a cursor is bound to the order it was minted in)
  - since (string, optional): wt_ id of a trade a previous call returned; answers only the trades recorded after it, in commit order, so a trade recorded late still arrives. Poll with the first trade of the last answer that had trades and deduplicate on id; recent order only
  - condition_id (string, optional): One market's large trades, by exact raw provider condition_id; not with event_slug or since

The page carries data_quality beside data: status, as_of (the oldest clock the page rests on) and field_groups. fresh and stale both mean tracked and clocked; stale means as_of is older than max_age_s, the refresh budget of the group writer. Neither is a tolerance: compare as_of with your own. unknown means this read cannot date that group, never that it is recent.

tools.name: get_edge_hunter
tools.description: Read the Max-only Edge Hunter API at https://0xinsider.com/sports/edge. Pro receives 403 forbidden with reason max_plan_required. One view selector offers board (default), full signals and cohort observations. All views accept kind sports|esports (omission covers both), sports, leagues, market_types, condition_ids, event_slugs, series_slugs and legacy category. Array selections accept 1..100 supplied values before deduplication, including comma-separated values inside a value; repeat REST query keys or supply MCP arrays. Lists match OR; axes match AND. Canonical sports and machine league identities normalize case-insensitively; market types and event/series slugs are exact case-sensitive provider strings. category=NFL selects the Football bucket; leagues=[nfl] selects NFL. category=sports, in any casing, reads as kind sports and echoes both; with kind esports it is a 400. Selection precedes the cap or pagination and appears as normalized selection beside the result fields; changed selections cannot share cursors or ETags. Every row carries nullable market_context with nullable league, series_slug, market_type and metadata_updated_at for authoritative filter discovery; metadata_updated_at is the local canonical writer clock, not provider observation time. Selected reads fail closed with 503 read_model_warming if frozen sidecar readiness is absent. Board defaults stay B grade floor, 30 rows and 48-hour horizon; min_grade S/A/B and limit clamp 1..30 are configurable, total is before the cap, with both current outcome quotes. Signals use min_grade default B, horizon default 12/clamp 1..48, limit default 20/clamp 1..100 and cursor, retaining token_id, all ranked/holder/directional/category-skill fields and clocks. Grade floor requires a holder at that grade or better without removing other holders. Observations require cohort wider_holder|in_play|emerging_pile, accept limit/cursor, and retain full observation rows, snapshot_as_of, degraded, source-generation/category funnel diagnostics and REST meta. With cohort wider_holder, admission most_held_48h opts in to the most-held selection instead: per sport, up to 8 wider_holder markets kicking off within 48 hours, most indexed_graded_holders first (on every row: S, A and B wallets in the 0xinsider index on either outcome, unlike graded_holders, the piled side of the provider's holder page), then volume, then soonest kickoff, at most 4 per event, recomputed every refresh and not held; rank orders the rows by directional_rank_score, not by either count; every row's admitted_by is most_held_48h, the response echoes admission, and its funnel, coverage and degradation describe that selection. admission most_held_48h_by_type requires market_types and runs that rule within each named type, per sport and market_context.market_type, so a type whose markets hold fewer wallets than team-win markets still gets up to 8 places (soccer totals: market_types [totals], category Soccer); its rows carry admitted_by most_held_48h_by_type, it has no departures, and a type not asked for in 30 minutes answers 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After 45 while the next refresh computes it. Required degradation_reasons names each cause with its canonical sport or null for a generation-wide cause. Degradation and coverage input_markets/capacity_limited_markets/emitted_observations/incomplete_holder_markets describe the whole all-sports generation and remain unchanged by selectors. coverage.selected_observations counts matching selected cohort rows before pagination; returned_observations counts this page. Intentional capacity_limited admission does not itself degrade a snapshot, and pagination cannot recover excluded markets. not_configured upcoming supply is not a provider failure. A selected funnel with no failure terminals does not prove the shared generation healthy. A legacy category value that cannot resolve to a sport retains its zero-work empty result: all six counts are zero and reasons are empty without reading the all-sports snapshot, so those values do not establish its health. Observation horizon stays 48h with 12h in-play kickoff lookback and 30s live snapshot ceiling; after one missed refresh, observations serve the last snapshot up to 45s longer with its age in meta.cache_age_s, and a second miss in a row returns 503; funnel accounting is not a league/type/ID selection census. All public views read warmed generations only; missing or stale readiness returns 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After 5. Advanced views use private,no-cache with REST/SDK ETag/304 helpers; board uses private,no-store and has no ETag/pagination. Invalid mode-specific parameters return 400. Price marks are market midpoints, not wallet entry prices; volume is shares. Null/db_only/degraded identify unavailable or weaker evidence. Analytics is not an order instruction.

tools.name: list_games
tools.description:
The fixture list: one coherent game per row, so an agent never has to assemble a game from market searches and team-name matching. Each row carries both sides with their provider ids and live scores, the UTC kickoff, the provider's own status, the esports series format, a tennis game's tournament edition (tier, place, venue time zone, draw and dates), and the game's winner markets (the moneyline, or a soccer game's three 1X2 legs) with their condition_id, outcome token ids and provider moneyline prices. A game's spreads, totals and player props are not on the row: list_game_markets lists every market of one event_slug. Ordered by kickoff, then event_slug; games whose kickoff the provider has not published sort last. For what is on now, pass window=now: without it the list is the whole catalog and starts at the oldest game still open, which can be weeks old.

Args:
  - sport (string, optional): canonical bucket, case-insensitive, with - and _ read as a space (table-tennis and Table Tennis are one bucket). Omitted means every covered sport
  - league (string, optional): league tag as this list's coverage.leagues spells it (nfl, epl, cs2), case-insensitive
  - status (string, optional): scheduled, live, paused, ended, postponed, cancelled, suspended, delayed, or unknown. ended, cancelled and postponed also list finished games that have left the live board (freshness.source stored) for kickoffs in starts_after..starts_before, by default the 7 days before now; such a page can be short, or empty, while has_more is true, so follow next_cursor until has_more is false
  - starts_after / starts_before (string, optional): RFC 3339 kickoff bounds; a game with no published kickoff is excluded whenever either bound is set
  - window (string, optional): all (default, the whole catalog) or now: games the provider reports in play, plus any other game whose kickoff was at most 3 hours ago or is still to come, without ended, postponed or cancelled games
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20)
  - cursor (string, optional): opaque gms_v1_ cursor from next_cursor. It pins the page position, not a snapshot: the catalog is live, so a game added or removed between pages moves with it
  - expand (string or string[], optional): sharp_money adds each game's sharp_money, the object get_game_sharp_money returns, read from the sport board's cached aggregate (one board read per sport, so a page stays fast). A game the board did not evaluate reads status not_computed: call get_game_sharp_money for it. A sport whose aggregate could not be read reads status unavailable while the rest of the page is served. Pro and Max. settlement adds each winner market's settlement, the block list_game_markets serves (status observed, not_posed or unavailable; oracle_status, payouts, result outcome or split, the 50-50; resolved_at), from the same store: it never waits for Polymarket: a market we saw settle reads its recorded settlement, and any other market of a game not read lately reads unavailable while its read starts. Every plan. Pass both, as an array, for both blocks: the costs add

Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor, as_of, coverage and meta. Read coverage before reading an empty page: it names the sports and leagues this deployment serves and any scope whose source was unavailable for this read, so an unserved sport is never confused with a quiet night. A sport this deployment does not serve returns an empty page, not an error; a status outside the listed values is invalid_query (upcoming games are scheduled). status.state keeps postponed, cancelled, suspended and delayed distinct from a plain 'not live', and a kickoff in the past is never read as live on its own. Scores are the provider's own strings, because a set score and a run total are not both integers. Carries no sharp-money split unless expand is sharp_money, and no holder identity; holders stay on get_market_holders.

sport.description: Canonical sport bucket, case-insensitive, with - and _ read as a space; omitted means every covered sport. A bucket this deployment does not serve returns an empty page

league.description: League tag as this list's coverage.leagues spells it (get_coverage lists no leagues): nfl, epl, cs2. Case-insensitive

status.description: Keep only games in this state

starts_after.description: RFC 3339 instant; keep only games whose kickoff is at or after it

starts_before.description: RFC 3339 instant; keep only games whose kickoff is at or before it. Must be at or after starts_after

window.description: all lists the whole catalog. now lists what is on now: games the provider reports in play, plus any other game whose kickoff was at most 3 hours ago or is still to come, without ended, postponed or cancelled games

cursor.description: Opaque gms_v1_ cursor from next_cursor; it pins the page position (kickoff and event_slug), not a snapshot

expand.description: One value, or an array of both. sharp_money: add each game's event-level sharp money (the object get_game_sharp_money returns, from the sport board's cached aggregate), so no per-game call is needed. settlement: add each winner market's settlement, the block list_game_markets serves

tools.name: get_game
tools.description:
The same game object list_games returns, for one event_slug: both sides with their provider ids and live scores, the UTC kickoff, the provider's own status, the esports series format, a tennis game's tournament edition (tier, place, venue time zone, draw and dates), and the game's winner markets (the moneyline, or a soccer game's three 1X2 legs) with their condition_id, outcome token ids and provider moneyline prices. For the game's spreads, totals and player props, call list_game_markets with the same event_slug. The slug is the identity the live_sports_updated webhook pulse carries, so a receiver can read the full game straight from a pulse.

Args:
  - event_slug (string, required): the game's event slug, for example nfl-buf-nyj-2026-09-22. Matched case-insensitively

Returns: the game object with the envelope's meta. status.state keeps postponed, cancelled, suspended and delayed distinct from a plain 'not live'. Each game's own coverage reports whether scores, competitor provider ids and the schedule were available: when competitors reads labels, do not join on names. A slug outside the published coverage answers 404, including a real Polymarket event in a sport this deployment does not serve; list_games names what is covered. Each winner market carries settlement, the block list_game_markets serves (status observed, not_posed or unavailable; oracle_status, payouts, result outcome or split, the 50-50; resolved_at); it never waits for Polymarket: a market we saw settle reads its recorded settlement, and any other market of a game not read lately reads unavailable, and a read a moment later may answer. Carries no sharp-money split and no holder identity.

event_slug.description: The game's event slug, for example nfl-buf-nyj-2026-09-22; matched case-insensitively

tools.name: list_game_markets
tools.description:
Every stored Polymarket market of one event_slug: the moneyline, spreads, totals, team totals, half and quarter lines, player props and the rest, plus the markets of the event's child events (a soccer game's exact score, halftime result and more-markets events), each with its own event_slug. Each row carries the condition_id, the provider's sports_market_type and groupItemTitle, the provider's typed line and, when stated, the outcome index it belongs to, both outcome labels with their CLOB token ids, active or closed status, and settlement: how Polymarket's oracle settled or is settling the market (status observed, not_posed or unavailable; oracle_status, the provider lifecycle state such as proposed, disputed or resolved; settled; payouts, micro-USDC per share per outcome index; result outcome or split, the 50-50; winning_outcome_index; was_disputed; resolved_at, null on a resolved UMA question row, which carries none; oracle_updated_at, Polymarket's last_update_timestamp, its latest lifecycle change and never a resolution time: on a resolved UMA question row, when UMA's answer settled the question; expected_settlement_time and settlement_time_basis; proposed_answer for a pending round; observed_at, on a settled market when we first saw the settlement, which never moves; a null is unknown). Ordered by sports_market_type, then line, then condition_id. Pass a condition_id to get_market_holders, get_market_flow or get_market_snapshot.

Args:
  - event_slug (string, required): the event slug from list_games, get_game or a search_markets result, for example nba-bos-orl-2026-11-01. Matched case-insensitively. Live, upcoming and settled events all answer
  - sports_market_type (string, optional): comma-separated provider market types to keep, case-insensitive (spreads, totals, points, first_half_totals). Omitted keeps every type; an unknown type returns an empty page
  - status (string, optional): active, closed or all (default all)
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20)
  - cursor (string, optional): opaque gmk_v1_ cursor from next_cursor, sent with the same filters
  - expand (string[], optional): sharp_money adds each row's sharp_money: status (computed, not_computed or unavailable; the first read of a game can be unavailable while its split is built, so retry after a few seconds), trader_count, per-outcome usd and S/A/B wallet counts, and money_as_of, the game page's per-line split. quotes adds each outcome's quote, the figures get_market_snapshot reads, for the whole page in one cache read and on every plan: status (observed; no_orderbook when the provider confirmed the outcome has no book; unavailable when nothing is cached yet, every figure null: the read starts covering the page's open markets, so read again after a few seconds), price (0 to 1, the price Polymarket shows) with price_basis (midpoint when the best bid and ask are at most $0.10 apart, else last_trade) and price_observed_at, best_bid and best_ask with book_observed_at and book_source (clob_stream from the market websocket, clob_rest from a CLOB books read), book_depth_within_2c (bid_usd and ask_usd, the USD resting on each side within 2 cents of the midpoint, price times size, from the whole book; null when no depth is cached for the book), and book_unavailable_reason (null with a book; else cache_miss, cache_unavailable when we could not read the book from the cache (read again), no_orderbook, missing_provider_token_id, or stream_capacity: API reads already hold every live book they may open, so reading again does not help until fewer markets are read). A null figure is one the cache does not hold, but a null best_bid or best_ask beside book_observed_at is a side with no orders. It adds 1 to the cost. trading_terms adds each row's trading_terms from the market's Gamma record, on every plan: status (observed; not_listed when Gamma's market list returns no record for it; unavailable when no read is in hand yet, every figure null: read again after a few seconds), fees_enabled, fee_schedule (rate, exponent, taker_only and rebate_rate, the fraction of taker fees rebated to the resting maker), rewards_min_size (shares), rewards_max_spread (cents from the midpoint), reward_allocations (rewards_amount, rewards_daily_rate, start_date, end_date), seconds_delay (seconds before a newly placed marketable order can match), tick_size and min_order_size_shares (the smallest order the CLOB accepts, in shares, not USDC), with observed_at. Every figure is Polymarket's, never derived. It adds 1 to the cost

Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor, event_slug, families and meta. families lists every market type the event holds with its market and active counts, whatever the filters: read it first to choose a sports_market_type. A slug no stored market carries answers 404; an event outside sports and esports answers 404 with reason market_out_of_scope. Carries a price only with expand quotes, and no holder identity: get_game_holders reads the holders of several of these markets in one call.

event_slug.description: The game's event slug, for example nba-bos-orl-2026-11-01; matched case-insensitively

sports_market_type.description: Comma-separated provider market types to keep, case-insensitive: spreads, totals, points, first_half_totals. Omitted keeps every type; the response's families lists the event's types

status.description: Keep only active or only closed markets; default all

cursor.description: Opaque gmk_v1_ cursor from next_cursor, used with the same filters

expand.description: sharp_money adds each row's sharp-money split: side USD and S/A/B wallet counts per outcome (#32155). quotes adds each outcome's quote: the cached display price, best bid and best ask, each with its observation time (#32893). trading_terms adds each row's fee schedule, reward settings, order delay, tick and minimum order size in shares from its Gamma record, with its observation time (#32688, #32938)

tools.name: list_props
tools.description:
Player props across the catalog's games of one league, one row per market: player, stat and line. NFL files props on a game's -player-props and -first-td-scorer child events and NBA on the game event; this reads both, so a caller does not walk list_games and then each game's markets. Each row carries player.name (the provider groupItemTitle before its first ": ", as the event page shows it; null with player_unavailable_reason when the provider stored no title), stat (the provider sportsMarketType), line (null for a yes/no prop such as an anytime touchdown), title, group_item_title, both outcomes with labels and CLOB token ids, status, resolved_at, and the game's game_event_slug, starts_at and competitors. Polymarket does not name a player's team. Rows are ordered by game slug, stat, player, line.

Args:
  - league (string, required): league tag as list_games coverage.leagues spells it, for example nfl or nba
  - starts_after / starts_before (string, optional): RFC 3339 kickoff bounds; a game with no published kickoff is excluded whenever either is set
  - player (string, optional): part of player.name, ignoring case and accents (jokic matches Nikola Jokić)
  - stat (string[], optional): provider sportsMarketType values to keep, for example passing_yards or points. Repeat the key or pass an array
  - status (string, optional): active (default), closed, or all
  - max_spread_c (number, optional): keep only props with an outcome whose cached best ask less best bid is at most this many cents (above 0, at most 100, steps of 0.01), from the same books expand=quotes serves. A prop whose book is not cached yet is left out and counted on coverage.rows_without_book; the board reads its league's books behind the response. A cursor never revisits a prop a page passed over, whether its book was wider or not cached yet, so when coverage.rows_without_book is above 0, read from the first page again after a few seconds to judge those props; the board reads books for active props only, so a closed prop, or one whose outcome has no provider token id yet, stays unjudged. When the book cache cannot be read for the first prop a page must judge, the read answers 503 with error.reason read_model_warming and Retry-After, not an empty page that repeats its cursor.
  - min_book_usd_within_2c (number, optional): keep only props with an outcome whose cached book holds at least this many USD on each side within 2 cents of its midpoint (bids at or above the midpoint minus 0.02, asks at or below the midpoint plus 0.02, price times size; a whole number from 1 to 10000000), the measure the market_price_moved webhook filter of the same name uses; expand=quotes serves the sums as book_depth_within_2c. With max_spread_c one outcome must meet both. A prop whose book or depth is not cached yet is left out and counted on coverage.rows_without_book, as for max_spread_c.
  - limit (number, 1-200, default 50)
  - cursor (string, optional): opaque prp_v1_ cursor from next_cursor, sent with the same filters
  - expand (string[], optional): quotes adds a quote to every outcome, the same object list_game_markets returns: the cached display price with its basis and observation time, the cached best bid and ask, and book_depth_within_2c. The board opens no live book: it reads the league's unstreamed books from CLOB behind the response, so a prop with no book yet reads book_unavailable_reason cache_miss (read again in a few seconds), and cache_unavailable when we could not read the book from the cache; book_source names who read the book (clob_stream or clob_rest); its price is fetched behind the response when no cache holds one, so a later read finds it. Adds 1 to the cost

Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor, league, as_of (when the game catalog was assembled), coverage and meta. Read coverage.sources_unavailable before trusting a short or empty page: it names each game catalog source (<sport>:<half>, as list_games coverage does) that could carry the league's games and did not answer for this read, and the page can be missing that source's games until a later read. With max_spread_c or min_book_usd_within_2c, coverage.rows_without_book counts the props this page passed over because no book (or, with min_book_usd_within_2c, no depth) was cached yet; it is null without either filter. A page can hold fewer than limit rows, or none, while has_more is true: a read that has not filled its page stops after about 100 ms of prop reads (a player filter that matches few rows) and resumes on the next page, and a child event out of scope is dropped. Follow next_cursor while has_more is true. An unknown league is invalid_query. A known league with no games in the window is an empty page.

league.description: League tag as list_games coverage.leagues spells it, for example nfl or nba

starts_after.description: RFC 3339 kickoff bound. A game with no published kickoff is excluded whenever either bound is set

player.description: Part of player.name, ignoring case and accents: jokic matches Nikola Jokić

stat.description: Provider sportsMarketType values to keep, for example passing_yards or points

max_spread_c.description: Keep only props with an outcome whose cached best ask less best bid is at most this many cents, in steps of 0.01; a prop with no cached book yet is left out and counted on coverage.rows_without_book

min_book_usd_within_2c.description: Keep only props with an outcome whose cached book holds at least this many USD on each side within 2 cents of its midpoint, a whole number from 1 to 10000000; with max_spread_c one outcome must meet both; a prop with no cached book or depth yet is left out and counted on coverage.rows_without_book

cursor.description: Opaque prp_v1_ cursor from next_cursor, used with the same filters

expand.description: quotes adds every outcome's cached quote, as on list_game_markets; a prop with no book yet reads cache_miss while the board reads its league's books from CLOB behind the response

tools.name: get_fair_price
tools.description:
The Polymarket fair price of one game outcome, to price a sportsbook bet against: the outcome's cached best bid, best ask, midpoint, spread in cents and USD resting within 2 cents of the midpoint on each side, the taker fee a buy at the ask pays, and fair.prob, the midpoint normalised over the market's outcomes (a soccer 1X2 leg over the three Yes midpoints). Name the outcome by condition_id and outcome, or by event_slug, market_type and outcome_label (plus line for a spread or total).

Args:
  - condition_id (string): the market's condition id; send with outcome
  - outcome (number): 0 or 1, the outcome index
  - event_slug (string): the game, as list_games returns it; send with market_type and outcome_label
  - market_type (string): moneyline, spread or total
  - outcome_label (string): the outcome's label as the market lists it, ignoring case, for example Commanders or Over
  - line (number): the exact line of a spread or total; required for those, refused for a moneyline
  - max_spread_c (number, above 0 and at most 100, default 3): the widest spread in cents that passes
  - min_book_usd_within_2c (number, 1-10,000,000, default 500): the USD each side must hold within 2 cents of the midpoint

Returns: data with status (ok, wide_spread, thin_book, stale_quote, closed or unavailable), failed_checks, the outcome, quote, fee (basis observed, disabled or assumed), fair (prob, prob_mid, decimal_odds, american_odds), game (start, started), the thresholds applied and as_of. Read status before using fair.prob: anything but ok means the midpoint is not fit to price a bet. A value the cache does not hold is null, never 0.

condition_id.description: The market's condition id; send with outcome

outcome.description: The outcome index, 0 or 1; send with condition_id

event_slug.description: The game, as list_games returns it; send with market_type and outcome_label

market_type.description: moneyline, spread or total; send with event_slug

outcome_label.description: The outcome's label as the market lists it, ignoring case, for example Commanders, Over or Draw

line.description: The exact line of a spread or total, for example -3.5 or 222.5; required for those, refused for a moneyline

max_spread_c.description: The widest spread in cents that passes (default 3)

min_book_usd_within_2c.description: The USD each side must hold within 2 cents of the midpoint (default 500)

tools.name: list_settled_markets
tools.description:
Game markets Polymarket settled, as 0xinsider recorded them, oldest first: one row per market per settled state, the same object the market_settled webhook delivers as data. Use it to catch up on settlements after downtime, as a pull alternative to the webhook (keep next_cursor and call again with it), or to find one market's or game's settlement by condition_id or event_slug. tools.name: get_game_sharp_money
tools.description:
Where the graded money sits on a whole game, in one read: the S, A and B grade wallets' USD on each side (home, away and, for a 1X2 game, draw) summed across the game's markets, each side's integer share of it, the leader, and wallet counts by grade, plus the backend's verdict on the split. The same aggregate the game page on 0xinsider renders, so the two cannot disagree. Use it instead of paging get_market_holders per market and summing.

Args:
  - event_slug (string, required): the game's event slug, for example nba-bos-orl-2026-11-01. Matched case-insensitively

Returns: data with event_slug, status, lifecycle, verdict, allocation, total_usd, unallocated_usd, trader_count, holders_partial, outcomes[] (side, label, usd, pct, is_leader, wallets.s/a/b; side is the provider's own home/away designation of the team, or draw, and null when the provider designates neither), computed_at, money_as_of and at_kickoff, plus meta. Every aggregate field is null unless status is computed, except lifecycle and at_kickoff, which describe the game; null means unknown, never zero. verdict.kind is no_sharp_money, all_on, split, leans (label, pct), leans_over_price (label, divergence_pts: how many probability points the money share sits above the price), no_clear_lean, unavailable (money exists but cannot be attributed) or withheld (the money is published but no directional claim is supported). When allocation is degraded, outcomes sum to total_usd minus unallocated_usd and carry no pct or leader. holders_partial true means a market's holder list was a capped page, so counts and dollars cover part of the holders. lifecycle live is a game before its scheduled start. lifecycle in_play is a game past its scheduled start, or reported live, and not over, a postponed or cancelled game included; get_game's status says whether it is being played. Its outcomes keep usd and wallets but carry no pct or leader, and verdict is withheld, since its holders are valued at prices that follow the score, or a called-off game's 50-50 resolution. A game that is over but not settled returns lifecycle ended: outcomes keep usd and wallets but carry no pct or leader, and verdict is withheld, since its holders are valued at post-result prices. An in_play or ended game carries at_kickoff, the split as the site last recorded it before the scheduled start, valued at that moment's prices: as_of, verdict, total_usd, trader_count and outcomes[] (side, label, usd, pct, is_leader). at_kickoff is null on every other lifecycle and when no split with graded money was recorded before the start. A settled game returns its recap with lifecycle settled. A game whose aggregate is still computing answers 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After; read again then. A slug with no sports market answers 404. Pro and Max. Descriptive analytics, not an order instruction.

tools.name: search_markets
tools.description:
Search prediction markets by keyword. Returns one market per matching Polymarket event, with status, category, platform and event_slug: the event's representative market: the market whose title is q, else a moneyline or winner market before an O/U, spread or alt line, so a game's spreads, totals and player props never appear as separate results. An event holding a market whose title is q (case-insensitive) ranks first whatever its date, so a pasted market title returns that market first. A game is one result: Polymarket's polyv2 copy of a game (event_slug polyv2-nba-lal-phx-2026-11-15 for nba-lal-phx-2026-11-15) is left out when the game itself is stored, as get_game does. Supports cursor pagination: pass next_cursor from the previous page with the same q, status and category to read the next page; stop when has_more is false. Args:
  - q (string, required): Search query
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20): Max results per page
  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor from the previous response's next_cursor
  - status (string, optional): Filter by status: "active", "closed", or "all" (default "all")
  - category (string, optional): Filter by category. One category such as Basketball or Esports; the word sports is rejected, so omit category for every sports and esports market

tools.name: get_pick_of_the_day
tools.description:
Get the published Pick of the Day selections for today, or for a past product day with `date`, or one pick of any day with `pick_id`, and their recorded facts. Pro opens five selections in total: the explicitly designated free selection plus the first four non-free selections in publication order. Max opens every available daily selection, up to twenty-five. Read entitled `picks` in `publication_order` order; use stable decimal-string `pick_id` for identity, not deprecated `pick_rank`. `is_free_selection` designates account access; `supersedes_pick_id` is deprecated and always null. `locked_picks` lists extra unresolved slots with only pick_rank and required_tier=max; game identity, identifying clocks and backed facts are omitted. Each full pick carries the matchup, its game's start (kickoff, RFC 3339 UTC, the time the site shows), backed side (pick_outcome_label), recorded publication price and return on the flat $1,000 stake (`stake_usd`, `return_usd`; `return_per_100` keeps the literal $100 basis), available holder facts, top grade, CLV capture status and backend-provided thesis. `scheduled_picks` contains entitled scheduled slots with release_at and kickoff; unauthorized slots appear in identity-free locked_picks instead. No market identity is revealed before publication. Withdrawn picks are omitted from current and dated recommendations, the archive and its statistics, even after market settlement. The public ledger retains every published commitment under its original identity and proof bytes. A sealed full pick names its proof: commitment_hash, sealed_at, ledger_url (the day's file in github.com/0xinsider/picks) and committed_kickoff, the start the commitment bound, which differs from kickoff when the game moved after release. game_start_time repeats kickoff; holders_observed_at and records_as_of date the listed wallets when the pick's release read is stored.

With `date`, the tool reads that past day's slate as the dated web page shows it, under the same tier rule, with no scheduled_picks. A past day with no published pick returns not_found with param date; a past day does not change, so do not retry it. A date after today is a bad_request.

For today, when no active pick is available, the tool returns reason pick_not_released and retry_at. Schedule the next read from the returned retry guidance or an entitled scheduled slot's release_at instead of polling. While today's list can still grow, the response carries more_picks_until, the instant until which another pick can still be added; it is absent once the day is final. A later pick is possible, not promised. An entitled published pick whose holder proof is not readable appears in `proof_pending_picks` (pick_rank, release_at, kickoff, retry_at), while `picks` contains readable picks. The tool returns read_model_warming only when no entitled published pick has readable proof. If only Max-locked selections have published, a successful state=none response carries picks=[], pick_count=0, locked_picks and an upgrade action.

The default view=summary lists each entitled pick in about 600 characters: pick_id, publication_order, is_free_selection, matchup, category, event_slug, polymarket_url, token_id, pick_outcome_label, outcome, backed_price, stake_usd, return_usd, unit_score, top_grade, holder_count, backed_side_share, sharp_positioned_usd, clv_status, clv_pct, release_at, kickoff, game_started and game_ended, with the disclaimer once and the same scheduled_picks, proof_pending_picks, locked_picks and more_picks_until. holder_count and top_grade count only the S and A grade wallets a pick lists, while backed_side_share and sharp_positioned_usd count every grade it lists (S, A and B since 2026-08-12): a pick that lists only B grade wallets reads holder_count 0 and no top_grade beside a positive sharp_positioned_usd, and its display_holders, read with pick_id, name those wallets. Each display_holders item's after_release says what that wallet did after release, beside its release shares: held, added, reduced or exited before the game, redeemed after settlement, or unavailable, with shares_change and last_change_at. A null held flag means not measured, never false. A page reads a fixed share of the history, so with narrow filters it can hold fewer than limit items, even none, while has_more is true: follow next_cursor until has_more is false.

Args:

  - event_slug (string, optional): One Polymarket event (game)

  - since/until (string, optional): RFC3339 bounds on episode_started_at, since inclusive, until exclusive

  - cursor (string, optional): next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters
